topics.title: 17.1.2 Choosing Queue or Log Behavior Deliberately
topics.summary: A work queue commonly distributes jobs among consumers, with acknowledgement controlling when work is considered handled under the broker’s rules. topics.summary: Consider three events: receive message, commit effect, acknowledge delivery. A crash before commit should leave the message eligible for later processing. topics.summary: A temporary database outage may justify redelivery. A malformed schema version, violated domain invariant, or permanently unauthorized action may not improve with another identical attempt. Repeatedly delivering a poison message at the front of a queue can block otherwise valid work.

A dead-letter queue is not a disposal bin. Someone must own retention, inspection, redrive authorization, and the risk that an old message’s meaning has changed.

blocks.text: Bound retries by count, time, or operational policy appropriate to the work. Interactive RPCs often have a caller deadline. Durable workflows can have longer recovery horizons, but they still need a terminal or escalation policy. “Retry forever” can hide a permanent defect for months while accumulating backlog.

blocks.text: The simple HarborDispatch dispatcher retains pending work and retries its fixed worker. It has no persistent quarantine state and processes bounded batches in row order. A permanently failing early operation can therefore impair later progress. This is a documented extension requirement, not silently presented as a full broker scheduler.

topics.title: 17.3.1 Separating Delivery Order from Completion Order
topics.summary: Two messages can be delivered in order and complete out of order when processed concurrently. If event 2 depends on event 1’s committed effect, a consumer pool must preserve that dependency or reject/defer the second transition. A FIFO input queue alone does not guarantee FIFO effects.

Partitioning by entity can make per-entity ordering easier while allowing parallelism across entities. The partition key must match the state that needs sequencing. Routing related events under different keys can erase the intended ordering boundary.

A version check can make stale updates harmless or explicit. For example, an entity expecting revision 6 should not blindly apply revision 8 as if revision 7 had been seen. The policy may fetch missing state, buffer within a bound, or treat events as snapshots rather than deltas. Those choices produce different recovery behavior.

Avoid asserting a global total order unless the application requires and implements one. It can become an expensive coordination point. Many systems need only per-account or per-job ordering plus explicit dependencies between a smaller set of operations.

reading.title: Engineering case — Advance a consumer checkpoint without skipping unfinished work
paragraphs: A log consumer receives offsets 40 and 41 and processes them concurrently. Offset 41 finishes first. The consumer records its next position as 42 and then crashes while offset 40 remains unfinished. On restart, beginning at 42 skips work that never committed.

A checkpoint describing a contiguous completed prefix must not advance past a gap. The consumer can track completed offsets and move the checkpoint only when every earlier required offset has completed under its effect contract. Alternatively, it can serialize processing where the throughput and ordering requirements permit.

The effect transaction also matters. If processing offset 40 updates an external database and the checkpoint is stored independently, a crash between those operations still creates a duplicate or loss window. A durable inbox keyed by event identity can make replay safe, while a supported transactional log-processing facility may atomically coordinate a narrower set of outputs and offsets.

Do not confuse offset 40 with the event’s universal identity. Exporting and replaying the event through another topic can assign it a different position. If duplicate effects must be recognized across that path, preserve a domain event identifier rather than relying only on the original transport coordinate.

Partition ownership can change during consumer rebalance. An old consumer may still have in-flight work when a new consumer begins. The application needs the broker client’s supported ownership protocol and, where necessary, effect-side deduplication or fencing. A local thread stop request is not proof that every external action has ceased.

A deterministic test can represent offsets 40 and 41 as two task states. Complete 41 first and verify that the contiguous checkpoint remains at 40. Then complete 40 and advance to 42. Add a restart between those transitions and verify replay of the unfinished work without duplicating already retained effects.

The companion does not run this broker scenario. Its direct dispatcher has one sequential delivery owner, which avoids this particular offset gap while limiting concurrency. The case shows what new state would become necessary when increasing parallelism in a log-based adapter.
